writer: an independent agent that saw only the ten questions (a separate agent; it read no file and no example, only the ten practice questions)
use: An evaluation set for the business-examples search (30.18): never indexed, never tuned on; each version names the pattern its question was written for.

versions.text: A hospital network handles about 3.5 million billing submissions a year, and nobody has ever marked which of them were abusive. How would you pick the first 400 bills for the auditors to open, and how would you show that this shortlist beats the checks the billing office already runs?

We get millions of payment requests and we have never kept track of which ones turned out to be dishonest. My team can look at a few hundred to start with. How do we decide which ones to look at first, and how can I tell whether that list is any better than the checks we use today?
prioritize suspicious records with no known bad cases, beat existing checks

A telecom operator has 85,000 flagged SIM-swap events, but about 72,000 of those flags were raised by its automatic alert logic and never confirmed by an investigator. How should training and evaluation be set up so the classifier picks up real account takeovers instead of simply copying the alert logic?

Most of the examples we would teach the system from were marked 'bad' by our own automatic checks, not by a person who actually looked into them, roughly six out of every seven. How do we teach it, and then check it, so that it learns what real cheating looks like rather than just repeating what our checks already say?
most outcome tags generated by heuristics: how to train and evaluate honestly

A logistics company wants its damaged-parcel detector to flag at least 90 percent of the shipments that really arrive broken, but the depot's inspection crew can open only 250 packages per shift. How do you choose the score cutoff, and what do you do when both demands cannot be met at once?

Leadership says we have to stop nearly every dishonest case, at least 19 out of 20, but my checkers only have time for about 300 files a day. Where do we draw the line on which files get sent to them?
score cutoff meeting a required hit rate under fixed daily review capacity

An online marketplace believes a single seller is quietly operating around 60 storefronts under different names. Across 8 million seller profiles, how can it discover which shops belong to the same operator without checking each profile against every other one?

We think one individual is hiding behind dozens of separate customer profiles with us. We have millions of profiles in total, far too many to hold each one up against all the others. How do we find the ones that really belong to the same person?
find sibling profiles across millions of records without all-pairs matching

A utility's meter-tampering detector used to be right about 3 out of 4 times it raised an alert; over six weeks that fell to under half. How would you work out whether the incoming readings changed, whether the way people tamper changed, or whether the original evaluation was flattered by information that was not really available at the time of the alert?

Our warning system used to be right about four times out of five when it raised a flag. Within a month it is barely better than a coin toss. How do we figure out whether the customers coming in are different now, whether the behaviour we are trying to spot has changed, or whether the system only looked good before because it was accidentally peeking at answers it should not have had?
alert accuracy dropped sharply in weeks: input shift, behaviour change, or leak?

A school district superintendent types into the assistant: 'Why did enrollment drop 8% this autumn compared with last year?' What checks need to run before the assistant is allowed to display its explanation?
If one of our directors asks the company's AI helper why sales went down by about a tenth last quarter, what has to be confirmed behind the scenes before it is allowed to give them an answer?
verify assistant's explanation of a quarterly sales decline before displaying
An airline's automated fare tool recommends cutting ticket prices by 40% on 1,500 routes. What safeguards keep that change from going live on its own?
Our software has proposed knocking about a third off the price of a couple of thousand items. What prevents it from just going ahead and doing that without anyone signing off?
approval gate before AI-proposed bulk price cuts go live

In a hospital, one department wants AI to read patient intake forms, another wants it to sort the messages arriving through the patient portal, and a third wants to predict how many beds will be needed next month. What kind of technique suits each of these, and why?

Three of my departments all want 'AI': one to deal with the supplier bills we receive, one to handle the flood of customer messages, and one to work out how much stock we will need. Should they all get the same thing, or does each need something different, and why?
matching AI approach to document extraction, message triage, and forecasting

A regional utility holds each household in five separate systems (billing, outage reporting, field service and two legacy platforms), each with its own account number. How can it create a single household record while keeping the dashboards and monthly reports that already depend on those systems working as before?

The same client shows up in four of our systems, and each one knows them by a different number. We want one place that shows everything about each client, but the finance and sales reports people rely on today must keep giving the same results. How do we do that?
merge client records across systems with different keys, keep reports intact

A city transit authority's analytics group has received 20 requests for data projects from different departments but only has the staff to deliver 6 this year. How should it decide which ones to take on, and which pieces can be built once and shared across them?

We have been asked for around a dozen and a half projects, and realistically my people can do about a third of them. How do I pick which ones to do, and what can we build once and use again across several of them?
prioritize many analytics requests with limited team, share common components
